event.summary: Host-backed fixture cleanup can SIGKILL a recycled, unrelated process group
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: running supervisor tests can kill unrelated same-user processes if a host-backed fixture runtime exits and its old process-group number is reused before the fixture is dropped. Details: this patch extends OwnedRuntime to child: Option<Child> (22527-22540) and adds host-backed registrations containing child: None and only group: pid (start_in_host, 22802-22810). teardown (22545-22551) still unconditionally calls kill_process_group, which issues libc::kill(-(group as i32), SIGKILL) with no identity/liveness check (22582-22588). The old justification at 22539-22544 relied on an unreaped direct child reserving its PID; it holds only for Some(child). A host actively reaps its child with waitpid(WNOHANG) on each event-loop iteration (crates/terminal-host/src/host.rs:347,454-474), explicitly releasing its PID for reuse (host.rs:761-766). Nothing in OwnedRuntime keeps that identity reserved. A reachable natural exit is spawn_claude_runtime's sh wrapper, which waits for an internal reporter whose own sleeper lasts only 25 seconds (core.rs:22726-22730,22847-22857); the busy-claim test additionally kills that reporter while retaining the fixture. Once that group has ended, later same-user process creation can reuse the number; fixture teardown then signals that replacement group. An assertion panic or cancellation still invokes OmpAdmission::drop (23241-23254), without verifying the root remains its own. Contract: .agents/test-authoring.md requires establishing peer liveness before relying on it during teardown; SPEC_impl.md Terminal host explicitly permits using a child as kill root only while alive and matching its pinned start identity (2120-2127). Root machine-sharing rules forbid touching processes not started by this run. Suggested fix: retain the host terminal plus the pinned child ProcessIdentity and use identity-checked teardown; never signal a stored bare group after the leader has been reaped. Preserve reporter cleanup while the owned group is still identifiable. Suggested bucket: highest, because the established primitive can signal an unrelated user's same-account process group, causing loss of running work; this consequence is not confined to test tooling. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source-level identity-lifetime defect; occurrence requires PID/process-group reuse before fixture teardown and has not been observed or reproduced. No claim of an observed unrelated kill. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Material caveats: test-only code, no shipped session cleanup defect claimed; existing direct-child Some variant retains its old unreaped-child protection until try_wait reaps it. Source investigation checked host reaping, fixture registration, runtime script lifetime, unconditional drop path, and group-signalling implementation. No execution performed.

event.summary: Host-backed fixture cleanup can SIGKILL a recycled, unrelated process group
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Synthesis revision: distinguishes leader reaping from actual empty-group/session lifetime and supplies a complete conditional interleaving. TLDR: supervisor tests can kill unrelated same-account work if the fixture's entire old group/session ends and its number is reused while the test still retains its cleanup guard. The earlier finding's strongest consequence is retained; leader reaping alone is not sufficient evidence of reuse. Source sequence: (1) claude_report_survives_the_former_claim_deadline invokes spawn_claude_runtime (core.rs:21518); that starts sh -c 'sh internal hook --vendor claude & ...; wait' (22847-22856). The host child calls setsid before exec (terminal-host/src/spawn.rs:555-580), so its PID P is also its PGID and SID. The terminal host itself has separately called setsid (spawn.rs:143-146), and therefore is not a member retaining the child's group/session. (2) start_in_host records OwnedRuntime { child: None, group: P } (core.rs:22806-22814), then awaits store.session at 22815-22820 and the session-map lock at 22825-22828 with no guard-lifetime or child-lifetime bound. A permitted interleaving delays this test task after guard registration while the separate host and its child processes continue. (3) The internal reporter script is only '#!/bin/sh
sleep 25
' (22725-22731). On its natural completion the inner shell waits/reaps its sleeper then exits; the outer shell's explicit wait reaps the reporter then exits. If a shell optimizes its final external command, that removes a process rather than adding an unbounded descendant. This normal-completion route leaves no orphaned sleeper or un-reaped reporter prerequisite. The host promptly reaps the outer child via waitpid(WNOHANG) (terminal-host/src/host.rs:347,454-475). Now all members of P's group and session have ended and been reaped. A still-live or unreaped descendant would prevent this step: do not infer free P merely because the leader was reaped. The busy-claim test's explicit reporter kill at core.rs:21447-21454 by itself is NOT the proof that P is free; a surviving sleep/group member must first go. (4) After the group/session is truly empty and the leader has been reaped, a later fork may allocate P to an unrelated same-account child; that child may become group leader with setpgid(0,0) or setsid. Linux fork documentation explicitly excludes an existing PGID or SID from new PIDs, while setpgid/setsid allow the new PID to name its own group: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fork.2.html (DESCRIPTION), https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setpgid.2.html (DESCRIPTION and NOTES), https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setsid.2.html (DESCRIPTION). This establishes why live descendants prevent reuse, and why an entirely ended/reaped group has no such identity protection. (5) The test task resumes. Even if spawn_claude_runtime now fails its reporter-alive/parent premise (core.rs:22863-22871), unwinding drops OmpAdmission. Drop calls kill_owner (23241-23254), which drains the retained None guard (23048-23052). OwnedRuntime::teardown unconditionally calls kill_process_group(P) (22545-22551), issuing kill(-P,SIGKILL) without a start-identity or group-ownership check (22582-22587). That signal targets the unrelated replacement group, not the retired fixture. Contract: test-authoring requires peer liveness before relying on it during teardown; root machine-sharing rules forbid touching unrelated processes; SPEC_impl.md:2123-2126 ties a kill root to the pinned child's continuing identity. Suggested fix: retain the host/pinned runtime identity and make group cleanup conditional on proven ownership; preserve descendant cleanup without treating a bare retired PGID as a durable handle. Suggested bucket: highest proposed, because unrelated user-owned running processes can be killed; harm is not confined to test tooling. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source-level unsafe identity lifetime and source-supported conditional interleaving; not an observed event. Exact occurrence premise not established by repository source: a sufficiently delayed guard/task and enough concurrent process creation for P actually to be reallocated as another same-account PGID before that guard is dropped. These are scheduling/allocation conditions, not behavior this test forces. Available source establishes that nothing prevents them; it cannot establish that they occurred, their probability, or the host's numeric allocation sequence. Process-lifecycle/scheduler evidence from a real affected run would establish occurrence, but none was requested or collected and no reproduction was performed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Material caveats: test-only defect, no production session cleanup bug claimed; a live descendant retaining the old group makes the signal hit the owned group and does not demonstrate this failure. Direct Some(child) still reserves its unreaped leader until an actual wait/try_wait releases it. External checks were read-only primary Linux interface documentation, not execution.

event.summary: Terminal-less test documentation treats host loss as proof no program survives
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Discovery pass 2; promotes l3 from lead after useful source checks. TLDR: the changed predicate-test explanation tells maintainers that nothing can still run after a terminal host is lost, even though the implementation explicitly supports a program outliving its host. This is false lifecycle documentation, not an established runtime guard or cleanup defect. Changed doc at core.rs:17825-17830 calls an Exited row 'host-orphaned', then says 'nothing of it is running'. A terminal-less Exited row establishes that the terminal did not survive reconciliation, not that the program or its process tree has ended. Exact contrary source contract at hosts/terminal.rs:754-769: pinned_child_root handles 'an unavailable or ended host' and explicitly 'a child that outlived its host (one that ignored the hangup of a host killed outright)'. That code at :771-784 still returns the pinned running child in this case. terminal-host/src/host.rs:256-274 describes ending the host by closing the PTY, and its Shutdown branch is at :821-830; no synchronous all-programs-gone promise follows from host end. Current reload at core.rs:6924-6955 records ObservedExit for a Running row whose terminal is absent and retains no runtime; it has no surviving-host child identity from which to prove a HUP-ignoring child's death. The test itself at :17832-17857 only checks a pure terminal/outcome predicate with synthetic entries and does not establish the stronger no-survivors premise in its new prose. The useful test should remain, but its explanation should distinguish an unconfirmed launch, absence of tracked liveness evidence, and residual programs left for later process-tree cleanup rather than asserting that nothing is running. Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness). event.summary: Terminal-less test documentation treats host loss as proof no program survives
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Discovery pass 2 final source/attribution revision. TLDR: the rewritten predicate-test explanation tells maintainers that no program can still run after its terminal host is lost, contrary to the explicitly supported host/program lifecycle. This is inaccurate test documentation; no production guard bypass, cleanup failure or observed user harm is claimed. Exact changed explanation at core.rs:17825-17830: 'A rebooted (`Interrupted`) or host-orphaned (`Exited`) row also reloads with no terminal, and nothing of it is running'. The pure test at :17832-17857 exercises terminal presence/outcome only; it does not prove that stronger absence-of-program premise. Contrary source contract: hosts/terminal.rs:754-769 describes Delete's pinned_child_root as usable after an unavailable or ended host, specifically including 'a child that outlived its host (one that ignored the hangup of a host killed outright)'; :771-784 returns the still-running matching child. Host end is not child reaping: terminal-host/src/host.rs:256-264 returns from its serve loop and closes its owned PTY when its fields drop; the Shutdown branch :821-830 queues Goodbye/ending, with no group kill/wait. Its failure-before-readiness path separately calls abandon -> kill_child_group (host.rs:247-253; spawn.rs:196-215), demonstrating that guaranteed kill/reap belongs to failed start, not every running-host exit. Current reload core.rs:6924-6955 records ObservedExit for a Running row whose terminal is absent, with no live host from which it could learn a surviving child identity. Thus host-orphaned Exited is an absence-of-terminal/evidence boundary, not proof nothing remains running. Fix direction: keep this useful pure predicate test, but describe why an unconfirmed launch is conservatively treated as possibly live and distinguish absent tracked liveness from residual programs left for later process-tree cleanup. Whole-range attribution checked: exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a core.rs:20993-21001 already has the unqualified 'nothing of it is running' clause about tmux-orphaned rows. Do not claim this patch first introduced that generic overstatement or a new runtime policy. The assigned hunk explicitly replaces tmux-orphaned with host-orphaned and pane-probed with terminal-probed; in-range -G history finds only 1ed482d for that substitution. This newly teaches the invalid host-specific inference despite the retained host-child-survival contract. Pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db core.rs:17771-17776 retains that host wording, so later cleanup does not repair it. Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness about a lifecycle/test premise). Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss consequence from this explanatory text. Confidence: confirmed pinned source/contract and full-range wording comparison; no execution. proposed_drop: false for the newly rewritten host-specific claim; prior generic wording and pre-existing runtime behavior are disclosed, not used as an automatic out-of-range dismissal. possible_cover: no same-location/source responsibility in supplied neighbours; g130/l3 also discusses distinct status evidence, and g128/l1 is legacy consent rather than this no-survivors explanation. Material caveats: this does not demand that the pure predicate be widened or that cleanup behavior be changed. Correct absence-of-terminal classification and intentional survivor limits do not make the stronger explanatory promise true. All readily checkable source premises settled, no open l3 lead. event.summary: Host report fixture's reduced metadata does not bypass its admission or offer assertions
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Discovery pass 3. TLDR considered: the new host-backed report fixture publishes a reduced SessionEntry whose info.agent_kind remains Generic and whose host tag uses generation zero; a mismatched fixture could admit/refuse for the wrong agent or generation and weaken the migrated tests. Useful checks/results: start_in_host at core.rs:22776-22828 sets snapshot from the seeded row's launch and entry.generation from row.generation, even though its display-only info fields retain entry_with defaults (:19140-19161). report_conversation chooses kind and generation from entry.snapshot.kind and entry.generation (:15311-15313), never info.agent_kind, then checks vendor equality and report launch_generation (:15342-15369). host_agent_anchor uses the entry matching the row generation (:15826-15853). All host-start call sites were enumerated; OMP callers use seed_omp_session, which seeds generation 0 (:23061-23114), and the Claude caller explicitly seeds generation 0 before starting the runtime (:21480-21518). No caller reuses this host helper after advancing its row generation. The busy-claim helper additionally asserts generation 0 and sets both snapshot and info agent kind (:21386-21407). OMP report/offer assertions call fixture.report and fixture.offer: report supplies the seeded row to admit_hook_report (:23139-23166); offer calls session_snapshot (:23228-23237), which computes its integration and offer from the stored launch/capture/version (:7448-7477). Thus the reduced display metadata does not supply a competing wrong-kind or wrong-generation mechanism for these actual assertions. This is a narrow fixture-responsibility exclusion; it does not certify a full production-shaped SessionInfo or refute any separately reported cleanup/owner-exit issue. Suggested bucket: other (test fixture consideration). Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security or user-work-loss route from this fixture metadata.
